source.title: A Simple Model of Inference Scaling Laws

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and tests scaling with repeated inference attempts, not scaling of held-out pretraining loss with parameters, tokens, or training compute, nor the other listed versions. It cites neural scaling-law work as context.
record.gate_note: The paper's own results concern pass@k and reconstruction behavior across repeated inference trials. Its LLM curves are taken from Brown et al. (2024), so they are not rows. The VAE results are an adjacent inference-scaling finding, not a test of the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study models and measures how pass@k and an 'inference loss' scale with the number of repeated inference attempts. That variable is not parameters, tokens or training compute. Its LLM curves are refits of Brown et al. (2024) data. The cost plots are illustrations with chosen numbers. The only new measurement is a toy VAE's pass@k over repeated samples. None of V1–V7 names inference-attempt scaling, so the study cites training scaling laws as context only.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors propose two simple statistical models: a Beta distribution of per-sample difficulty, and power-law-correlated trials. Both yield pass@k and an 'inference loss' that decays as a power law in the number of attempts. The authors say the models fit LLM curves taken from Brown et al. and a toy VAE experiment. They suggest future work combining this with training scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study models repeated-inference scaling rather than reproducing a training-scaling method.
record.method_sensitivity: The VAE coverage curves are shown for different reconstruction thresholds; the text does not state their individual values.

fits_no_version.finding: Pass@k over repeated stochastic reconstructions of a toy VAE (Fashion-MNIST, T=1.1) is approximated well by the effective-k model. Correlations between trials have eigenvalues that decay as a power law.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Coverage and inference loss under repeated inference attempts follow a predictable power-law form in the number of attempts k.

record.problems: The VAE experiment is a single described model and dataset setting; the plotted results do not provide numerical coverage values or uncertainty estimates. The LLM coverage curves discussed are cited from prior work, not newly measured here.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. LLM pass@k curves and illustrative compute-cost plots draw on results or fitted parameters from Brown et al. (2024), rather than new measurements by this study.

untested.parts: Pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or compute is not measured.
No extrapolation from small training runs to large ones.
No compute-optimal allocation between parameters and tokens.
No effect of architecture shape at a fixed parameter count.
The image VAE result concerns repeated inference attempts, not training-scaling variables.
Downstream pass@k is not related to model scale or pretraining loss.
No analysis of whether training-scaling exponents depend on setup or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The LLM fits (Figs 1–2) and the inference-cost plots (Fig 3) rest on Brown et al. (2024) data or on illustrative parameters, so they are correctly excluded as rows. The study is not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: Not tested: held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Not tested: predicting much larger training runs from smaller runs.
Not tested: compute-optimal parameter and token allocation.
Not tested: effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Not tested: the listed power-law claim across modalities or training regimes; the image VAE experiment concerns repeated inference attempts, not those scaling variables.
Not tested: downstream performance predictability from model scale or pretraining loss.
Not tested: dependence of the stated training-scaling exponents or compute-optimal split on setup or fitting choices.

rows.subject: VAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on the first 400 samples from the Fashion MNIST dataset; 1000 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Measured pass@k for repeated stochastic reconstructions and compared coverage curves with the effective-k prediction.

conditions.value: different ϵ values; individual values not stated

rows.measure: pass@k as a function of number of attempts k
rows.value: Theoretical predictions approximate the VAE pass@k results well.
rows.note: Figure plots separate threshold curves, but threshold values and numerical pass@k values are not stated in the text. This is an inference-attempt result, not a test of the listed training-scaling versions.
rows.check: The row measures VAE reconstruction pass@k against the number of inference attempts k, not loss against parameters, data or compute. Its 'observed' state refers to the paper's own effective-k model, not to any claim version. No baseline is given and no threshold values are stated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
